title: The four parts and their balances

blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Identify the four current-account components, classify transactions and calculate balances for a stated period.

blocks.heading: What the account records
blocks.text: The current account records transactions between residents and non-residents over a period, such as one year. Its four sections are trade in goods, trade in services, primary income and secondary income. A receipt from abroad is recorded as a credit; a payment abroad is a debit. A section balance equals receipts minus payments. Add the four section balances to obtain the current-account balance: a positive result is a surplus and a negative result is a deficit.

blocks.heading: Putting transactions in the right section
blocks.text: Goods are physical products: a Namibian seller exporting dried fruit to Botswana earns a goods credit, while imported machinery is a goods debit. Services include transport and tourism: a German visitor buying accommodation from a Namibian lodge purchases a service export, even though the visitor consumes it in Namibia. Primary income includes earnings from work and investments across borders, such as interest received from a foreign deposit or dividends paid to overseas shareholders. Secondary income includes current transfers without a corresponding good, service or asset received in return, such as money a worker abroad sends to family at home. Buying shares is different from receiving a dividend on them; the dividend is primary income, whereas the asset purchase belongs outside the current account.

blocks.heading: Four balances, one total
blocks.text: Use these invented annual figures, all in N$ million. Goods receipts are 120 and payments 150, giving 120 - 150 = -30. Services receipts are 40 and payments 20, giving 40 - 20 = 20. Primary income receipts are 8 and payments 12, giving 8 - 12 = -4. Secondary income receipts are 10 and payments 6, giving 10 - 6 = 4. The current account is -30 + 20 - 4 + 4 = -10: a deficit of N$10 million. A services surplus therefore can offset part of a goods deficit without eliminating the overall deficit. Calculate each section before combining them, and retain the minus signs.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: International specialisation in topic 6.1 and trade in topic 6.2 help explain these flows; topic 6.3 explains their currency conversion.
